review_notes: I read the whole file and its uses in IterationFaceCapacity and StoppedLineages. I also read SubdivisionMap.comp, comp_point and NodeMassMap.refl/comp in the sibling files. The existing @[simp] lemmas (refl_comp, comp_refl, transport_self, comp_stable_coord) are oriented sensibly and I saw no cycle or competing rule. The gap is that the `refl` and `comp` constructions have no projection simp lemmas, so a proof has to unfold them by name. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether `simp` could already close the `transport_node_eq_ancestor` base case without the unfolding, so the proposed lemmas are untested.

findings.excerpt:
subdivision := SubdivisionMap.refl (Φ i)
  level_parent _ := le_rfl
  stable y := StableNodeMap.refl (Φ i) y
findings.problem: The identity and composition constructions have no projection simp lemmas. Examples are `(SubdivisionMap.refl Φ).node = SupHom.id _`, `(SubdivisionMap.refl Φ).fibre _ = AffineMap.id ℝ _`, `(Transport.refl Φ L i).subdivision = SubdivisionMap.refl (Φ i)` and `(M.comp N).subdivision = M.subdivision.comp N.subdivision`. The file does mark `refl_comp`, `comp_refl` and `comp_stable_coord` as simp, so the simp set is only half built. The base case of `transport_node_eq_ancestor` then has to unfold the definitions by name with `simp [Transport.refl, SubdivisionMap.refl]`. Unfolding like this is brittle. It exposes the internal structure of the definitions to callers, and a client that reaches `.subdivision.node` of a `refl` or `comp` transport cannot normalise it with plain `simp`. The same gap shows in `IterationFaceCapacity`, which has to use `change (E.progress.subdivision.comp T.subdivision).node F.node = _` to see through `comp`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` projection lemmas proved by `rfl`: `SubdivisionMap.refl_node`, `SubdivisionMap.refl_fibre`, `Transport.refl_subdivision`, `Transport.comp_subdivision`, and optionally `Transport.lowParent_val : (M.lowParent y).val = M.subdivision.node y`. Combined with the existing `SubdivisionMap.comp_point`-style lemmas, the base case in `transport_node_eq_ancestor` should reduce to plain `simp` without the `[Transport.refl, SubdivisionMap.refl]` unfolding list. Downstream proofs could also rewrite `(D.transport hL h).subdivision` through `comp` without `change`. I did not check whether the existing `simp` call already closes that goal without the unfolding.
findings.benefit: Proofs about transports use stable named rewrite rules instead of unfolding definitions. The proof in `transport_node_eq_ancestor` becomes more robust. Later files such as `IterationFaceCapacity` can normalise `.subdivision.node` of composed or identity transports with `simp` instead of `change`.
